tool.name: Fixed-width to tabular
tool.description: convert fixed-width text columns to TSV
tool.command: fixed2tab --input '$input' --table '$table' --report '$report' --rejected '$rejected' #if str($geometry.mode) == 'columns': --columns '$geometry.columns' #elif str($geometry.mode) == 'widths': --widths '$geometry.widths' #end if --min-gutter $detection.min_gutter #if str($detection.record_width): --record-width $detection.record_width #end if #if str($detection.header_line): --header-line $detection.header_line #end if --encoding '$reading.encoding' --short-lines '$reading.short_lines' $output_shape.collapse_spaces --header '$output_shape.header' #if str($strictness.mode) == 'strict': --strict #if $strictness.allow_rejects: --allow-rejects #for $reason in $strictness.allow_rejects: '$reason' #end for #end if #end if

param.label: Fixed-width text file
param.help: Do not upload it with 'convert spaces to tabs': that destroys the column positions.

param.label: Column ranges
param.help: START-END[:NAME] separated by commas, for example 1-12:DATE,18-27:BEST_TIME. Positions start at 1, and both ends are included. The report of an earlier run prints this string: copy the part between the quotes.

validator.message: Write START-END or START-END:NAME, separated by commas. Names use letters, digits and underscores only.

param.label: Column widths
param.help: Read from position 1: N takes the next N positions as a column, N:NAME does the same and names it, and Nx skips N positions. For example 12:DATE,5x,10:BEST_TIME. A FORTRAN FORMAT such as 2X,I5,2X,F8.3 transcribes directly to 2x,5,2x,8.

validator.message: Write N, N:NAME or Nx, separated by commas. Names use letters, digits and underscores only.

param.label: Blank positions that separate two columns
param.help: Lower values give more columns, because a smaller blank run separates two columns. Higher values merge narrow columns.

param.label: Record width
param.help: Leave empty to detect it. Set it for a file whose trailing blanks were stripped.

param.label: Line with the column headings
param.help: Leave empty to detect it. Lines 1 to N are preamble and are not converted. 0 means that the file has no preamble. Required when short lines are padded.

param.label: Input encoding
param.help: Try latin-1 for byte-padded legacy output.

param.label: Lines shorter than the record width
param.help: Padding can make page numbers and footers into data rows, so rejecting is the default.

param.label: Reduce runs of spaces inside each cell to one space
Header row in the table
param.help: The column names are always in the report. A header row shifts the row positions by one for later steps.
param.option: Column names as the first row

param.name: mode
param.label: Fail the job when lines are rejected?

tool.help:
**What it does**
Converts a fixed-width text file into a tab-separated table. Legacy programs often write their results as aligned columns. Tools that split on a delimiter cannot read such files: a cell that contains spaces breaks into several cells, and a blank cell shifts every later field to the left.
The tool finds the column boundaries itself. A boundary is a run of character positions that are blank in every record. Usually, no settings are necessary.
-----
**Outputs**
Every successful run gives three datasets:
- **Table**: one row per record, cells separated by tabs. It has no header row unless you select one. - **Report**: what the tool detected, and how to correct it. - **Rejected lines**: every input line that the tool did not convert, as three columns: line number, reason and the line itself. It usually holds only the title and heading lines.
The table rows plus the rejected lines always equal the input lines, so no line disappears without a record.
-----
**Check and correct the result**
Read the report in this order:
1. **Reconciliation** must end in `[OK]`. 2. **Input** shows the record width and the line used as the header. 3. **Columns** lists each column with its range, name and sample values. 4. **Warnings** names what to change.
To correct a boundary or a name, find the section "Reproducing or correcting this geometry" in the report. Copy the text between the quotes, for example `1-12:DATE,18-27:BEST_TIME`. Select "Give the column ranges", paste the text, change only the wrong range or name, and run the tool again.
-----
**Upload hazard**
Do not upload the file with "convert spaces to tabs". That option destroys the column positions before the tool sees the data. A tab inside a record makes the job fail.
-----
**Exit codes**
A failed job shows its reason in the error message:
- 2: the parameters are not valid. - 3: the input cannot be used. It cannot be decoded, has a tab inside a record, is empty, or has no records. - 4: strict mode is on, and lines were rejected.
More information: [Running fixed2tab on a file, step by step](https://github.com/dasch-swiss/rdu-fixed2tab/blob/main/docs/running-fixed2tab.md)
